input_messages.content: Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.
It looks like my phone's status bar is showing the airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything else. What should I do next?
Okay, I’ve turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," and the battery is still at 80%. I still don’t have any service. What should I try next?
It says my SIM card is active and working. What does that mean? Is there something else I should try?

I ran the network status check. It says:

- Airplane Mode: OFF
- SIM Card Status: active
- Cellular Connection: no service
- Cellular Signal: none
- Cellular Network Type: none
- Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
- Data Roaming Enabled: No
- Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
- Wi-Fi Connected: No

I’m still not getting any signal at all. What should I do now?
The APN name on my phone says "broken," and there’s also something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means—should I change something?

If resetting the APN settings will help fix this, then yes, please go ahead and reset them. I just want to make sure—will this mess up anything else on my phone, like my photos or contacts? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Alright, the APN settings have been reset, but it says they’ll take effect after I reboot my phone. I’m a bit nervous—restarting won’t delete my photos or anything, right? Can you reassure me before I do this?

Okay, I’ve restarted my phone. Now the status bar shows full signal bars, 5G, and it says data is enabled. It looks like everything is working again! Thank you so much for your help—I was really worried there for a bit.

Thank you so much for your patience and reassurance. I really appreciate your help—technology can be so overwhelming for me sometimes! I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but for now, everything seems to be working just fine. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

simulator_guidelines:
# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?

To assist you with the "No Service" issue on your phone, I need to identify your account and line details first. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth for verification?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

{"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}

{"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 8.7, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}

Your line with phone number 555-123-2002 is active and not suspended. To diagnose the "No Service" issue, let's start by checking your phone's status bar to see what indicators are showing. This will help us understand if airplane mode is on, signal strength, and other relevant info.

Please run the check_status_bar diagnostic on your phone and tell me what it shows.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
It looks like my phone's status bar is showing the airplane icon, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything else. What should I do next?

The airplane icon indicates that Airplane Mode is currently ON, which disables all wireless communications including cellular service. To restore service, you need to turn Airplane Mode OFF.

Please use the toggle_airplane_mode action on your phone to turn Airplane Mode OFF. Let me know once you have done that.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I’ve turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," and the battery is still at 80%. I still don’t have any service. What should I try next?

Since Airplane Mode is off but you still see "No Signal" and "Data Disabled," let's check the SIM card status next to ensure it is properly recognized and active.

Please run the check_sim_status diagnostic on your phone and tell me what it shows.
Your SIM card is active and working.
It says my SIM card is active and working. What does that mean? Is there something else I should try?

Since your SIM card is active and working, the issue is not with the SIM itself. Next, let's check your phone's network status to see if mobile data is disabled and to get more details about the signal and network type.

Please run the check_network_status diagnostic on your phone and tell me the results.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

I ran the network status check. It says:

- Airplane Mode: OFF
- SIM Card Status: active
- Cellular Connection: no service
- Cellular Signal: none
- Cellular Network Type: none
- Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
- Data Roaming Enabled: No
- Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
- Wi-Fi Connected: No

I’m still not getting any signal at all. What should I do now?

Your phone shows no cellular signal or network type despite mobile data being enabled and airplane mode off. Since your line is active and not suspended, and your SIM is active, this could be a network or configuration issue.

Next, let's check your phone's APN (Access Point Name) settings to ensure they are correct for your carrier. Incorrect APN settings can cause no service issues.

Please run the check_apn_settings diagnostic on your phone and tell me what it shows.

Current APN Name: broken
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
The APN name on my phone says "broken," and there’s also something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means—should I change something?

The "broken" APN name indicates your phone's APN settings are incorrect, which can cause the no service issue. The MMSC URL is related to picture messaging and also needs to be correct.

I will guide you to reset your APN settings to the default for your carrier. After resetting, you will need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Please confirm if you want me to proceed with resetting your APN settings now.

If resetting the APN settings will help fix this, then yes, please go ahead and reset them. I just want to make sure—will this mess up anything else on my phone, like my photos or contacts? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Resetting the APN settings will not affect your photos, contacts, or any other personal data on your phone. It only restores the network configuration settings to the default for your carrier, which should help fix your service issue.

I will proceed with resetting your APN settings now.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, the APN settings have been reset, but it says they’ll take effect after I reboot my phone. I’m a bit nervous—restarting won’t delete my photos or anything, right? Can you reassure me before I do this?

Rebooting your phone will not delete any photos, contacts, or personal data. It simply restarts the device to apply changes and refresh all services.

Please go ahead and reboot your phone now to apply the APN reset. Let me know once your phone has restarted.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I’ve restarted my phone. Now the status bar shows full signal bars, 5G, and it says data is enabled. It looks like everything is working again! Thank you so much for your help—I was really worried there for a bit.

I'm glad to hear your phone is now showing full signal and 5G with data enabled! Your service should be fully restored for calls, texts, and data.

If you have any other issues or questions in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!

Thank you so much for your patience and reassurance. I really appreciate your help—technology can be so overwhelming for me sometimes! I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but for now, everything seems to be working just fine. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###
